title: Magic E / Silent E Rule (Vowel-Consonant-e)
objectives: Apply the Vowel-Consonant-e long vowel rule
Recognize silent e at word ends
Contrast CVC short vs VCe long vowel pairs

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: Magic E / Silent E Rule (Vowel-Consonant-e). Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner pronounces 'give' as /geɪv/ following the Magic E rule.
💡 Solution: Highlight 'give, have, love' as the top 3 silent-E exceptions to memorize.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Magic E / Silent E Rule (Vowel-Consonant-e)
1. Definition: Silent E at the end of a word jumps over one consonant to make the previous vowel say its long name.
2. Rule: Vowel + Consonant + e = Long Vowel sound (A=/eɪ/, E=/iː/, I=/aɪ/, O=/oʊ/, U=/juː/ or /uː/).
3. Why? Silent e was historically pronounced, and its loss left the preceding vowel lengthened.
4. How to recognize? Pattern: V + C + e at word end (cake, time, home).
5. Common examples: cake /keɪk/, time /taɪm/, home /hoʊm/, cute /kjuːt/, hop -> hope, tap -> tape, bit -> bite
6. Counter-examples: have, give, love, come, some, done, gone (high-frequency exceptions).
7. Exceptions: have /hæv/, give /gɪv/, love /lʌv/, come /kʌm/.
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing the final e sound aloud (*cake-y).
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Magic E is SILENT, but it makes the vowel SAY ITS NAME!
10. Key vocabulary: magic e, silent e, long vowel, VCe pattern, vowel name
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟢 A1
13. Associated Visual: 🪄 Magic wand jumping over the consonant to make the vowel say its name.
14. Key Takeaway: VCe = Long Vowel + Silent E!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Do you pronounce the 'e' at the end of 'cake'? (No, it is silent)
CCQ 2: What does the silent 'e' do to the letter 'a' in 'tape'? (Makes it long /eI/)
CCQ 3: Are 'have' and 'give' regular Magic E words? (No, they are famous exceptions with short vowels)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Transform short vowel CVC words into long vowel Magic E words:
🎯 Item: hop -> ? ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: hope /hoʊp/
🎯 Item: tap -> ? ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: tape /teɪp/
🎯 Item: bit -> ? ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: bite /baɪt/
